From 1.21, feature-gate EfficientWatchResumption is enabled by default. Every reflector will sync the bookmark from APIServer.

Etcd will notify bookmark to APIServer, and APIServer will notify bookmark to watch client. The etcd notify interval is 10 minutes by default, so different APIServers may have different bookmarks.

Please consider the following scenario.

APIServer A has bookmark 100, APIServer B has bookmark 110
The reflector in watch_based_manager listwatch from APIServer B, it will save 110 as LastSyncResourceVersion.
Suppose the reflector stoped and restarted, and it requests list to APIServer A with RV=110 , the list will fail due to TooLargeResourceVersionError, accompanied by a 3-second delay. It will attempt to retry 10 times, and finally reset the resourceversion to '' .

We can set experimental-watch-progress-notify-interval=5s in etcd to notify bookmark more frequently, but I think we should also improve the reflector behavior.

Here we can set reflector lastResourceVersion to '0' instead of old version. @liggitt WDYT?

> Here we can set reflector lastResourceVersion to '0' instead of old version. @liggitt WDYT?

Setting to 0 is not safe, that opts into receiving stale data.

> the watch will fail due to TooLargeResourceVersionError, accompanied by a 3-second delay. It will attempt to retry 10 times, and finally reset the resourceversion to '' .

The spots I'm seeing us handle TooLargeResourceVersionError look like they should request with resourceVersion="" on the very next request. Tracing why we're retrying 10 times seems like the thing to track down and resolve.

> Tracing why we're retrying 10 times seems like the thing to track down and resolve.

Yes, this appears to be a better solution.

issue_context.title: Reduce error "failed to sync secret cache: timed out waiting for the condition"
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

```
kubelet_pods.go:897] "Unable to retrieve pull secret, the image pull may not succeed." pod="default/xxxxx" secret="" err="failed to sync secret cache: timed out waiting for the condition"
```

When a pod reference a secret or configmap, kubelet will add watch in `WatchBasedManager`. If the secret idle time over 5 minutes, the kubelet will stop watch.

When a new pod which references the same secret  is assigned to this node, kubelet will restart the secret reflector and get secret with timeout 1 second. 
And the secret reflector will try to get secret with `resourceversion` ,but got `Too large resource version`. The failed get request delayed 3  seconds. Kubelet  will  get error `failed to sync secret cache: timed out waiting for the condition`.


### What did you expect to happen?

Reduce error "failed to sync secret cache: timed out waiting for the condition"

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1.  Create a pod with image pull "regsecret".
2. Wait for more than 5 minutes,  the reflector is stopped.  With bookmark events, the secret reflector resourceversion is larger than the secret self and
3. Create a new pod with image pull "regsecret", ensure the pod is assinged to the same node.

### Anything else we need to know?

It sounds like a temporary timeout when kubelet tries to sync the secret and it can recover soon.

review_comments: If so, why do we loop over it?
`objectCacheItem` has no information about key, we can't get by key from store.
exposing this significantly increases the risk something will set it incorrectly and make the reflector behave incorrectly... I really don't think we should do that.

resetting to the object resourceVersion risks triggering a "too old / gone" error.

what does the reflector do in the case of a "Too large resource version" error?

what does the reflector do in the case of a "Too old / gone" error?

> resetting to the object resourceVersion risks triggering a "too old / gone" error.

It shouldn't - the semantic that we're using is "NotOlderThan", so passing very old version isn't necessary bad (and in many cases it will actually be really old RV).

No matter what, we need a comprehensive tests to actually avoid future regressions.

> what does the reflector do in the case of a "Too large resource version" error?

We're effectively relisting from resourceVersion=""
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache/reflector.go#L525

> what does the reflector do in the case of a "Too old / gone" error?

if it's coming from list, the handler is the same as for too large:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache/reflector.go#L517

if it's coming from watch - we go back to relist (first from existing RV):
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache/reflector.go#L444

@wojtek-t When  the apiserver   Bookmark is old, it will retry 10 times with the cached Bookmark version  before relisting from resourceVersion="", each attempt will take 3 seconds. So pod starting delayed for 30 seconds.

> the semantic that we're using is "NotOlderThan", so passing very old version isn't necessary bad

if that's true, then I don't understand what issue this PR is trying to solve... wouldn't passing the old secret or bookmark version we saw last work properly?
plumbing ResourceVersion seems ok, but we also have to plumb ResourceVersionMatch if we're going to start using ResourceVersion so the *meaning* of resourceVersion is honored
